lines.why: Goods held for sale: operating.

lines.why: Prepayments and other operating items: operating.

lines.why: Assets used to produce and sell: operating.

lines.name: Operating lease right-of-use assets
lines.why: Leased stores, offices and equipment used in the business: operating.

lines.name: Goodwill
lines.why: Paid for acquired businesses: operating.

lines.why: Acquired technology, brands and customer relationships: operating.

lines.name: Equity-method investments
lines.why: Stakes in associated businesses, usually part of operations. Financial if held as an investment.

lines.name: Other non-current assets
lines.why: Other long-term operating items: operating.

lines.name: Accounts payable
lines.why: Owed to suppliers for operations: operating.

lines.name: Accrued liabilities
lines.why: Services and other costs not yet paid: operating.

lines.name: Accrued compensation
lines.why: Wages, bonuses and benefits earned but not yet paid: operating.

lines.name: Income taxes payable
lines.why: Taxes on operating income: operating.

lines.name: Current portion of long-term debt
lines.why: Borrowed money falling due within a year: financial.

lines.name: Long-term debt
lines.why: Bonds, notes and loans: financial.

lines.name: Operating lease liabilities
lines.why: Rent owed on leases used in the business: operating by default. Move it to financing to treat leases like debt (if the balance sheet has no lease line of its own, they sit inside other liabilities).

lines.name: Deferred tax liabilities
lines.why: Taxes on operating income deferred: operating.

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities
lines.why: Other long-term operating obligations: operating.

lines.name: Other current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current assets minus the current lines above: current assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current assets (total assets − current assets) minus the non-current lines above: assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current liabilities minus the current lines above: current liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current liabilities (total liabilities − current liabilities) minus the non-current lines above: liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

s.t: The sales of cigarettes represented approximately 64% and 61% of our consolidated revenue in fiscal 2026 and fiscal 2025, respectively.

Sales of candy, beverages, foodservice, groceries, health food products, paper products, health and beauty care products, and tobacco products represented approximately 36% and 39% of our consolidated revenue in fiscal 2026 and fiscal 2025, respectively.
During fiscal 2026, approximately 64% of our consolidated revenues came from the distribution of cigarettes, which generated approximately 17% of our consolidated gross profit.

While the Company sells a diversified product line, it remains dependent upon the sale of cigarettes which accounted for approximately 64 % and 61 % of the Company’s consolidated revenue during fiscal 2026 and fiscal 2025, respectively, and 17 % and 17 % of the Company’s consolidated gross profit during fiscal 2026 and fiscal 2025, respectively.

Our principal suppliers include Altria, RJ Reynolds, ITG Brands, Hershey, Kellanova, Kraft Heinz, Mars Wrigley, General Mills, Procter and Gamble, Ferrero and other major Consumer Packaged Goods and Foodservice suppliers.
However, we do participate in a number of programs designed by our major vendors to support in-stock positions of our key products.
There can be no assurance that we or the manufacturers we rely on as suppliers will be in compliance with all of these regulations.
The benefits of liability limitations and indemnities we are entitled to under the MSA do not apply to sales of cigarettes manufactured by non-MSA manufacturers.
Deep-discount cigarette brands are brands generally manufactured by companies that are not original participants to the MSA, and accordingly, do not have cost structures burdened by the MSA.
Since the MSA was signed, the category of deep-discount brands manufactured by smaller manufacturers or supplied by importers has grown substantially.

Both of our operating segments rely on distribution and transportation networks, which includes our drivers, our distribution center employees, and the networks of our suppliers and retail store delivery partners, to deliver products to us and our customers in a timely and cost-effective manner.
We expect that our principal sources of funds will be cash generated from our operations and, if necessary, borrowings under our revolving credit facilities or other debt financing arrangements.
We depend on the continued services and performance of our senior management and other key personnel.

We believe these targeted investments will be a competitive differentiator over time and will set the stage for future growth as major manufacturers and leading convenience store chains are increasingly relying on large distributors who can both cover wide geographic footprints and deploy unique merchandising and technology solutions.
